stories.title: Microsoft says 'not aware of any malicious activity' causing Outlook outage
summary: Microsoft services such as Outlook and Teams were disrupted for about 10 hours on Friday as the tech giant struggled to fix issues with some servers, hitting businesses and government agencies globally that use the popular platforms.
It also showed outages for several Microsoft services in the Asia-Pacific region, including India, Australia and Japan, early Friday local time.
The US House of Representatives said the outage impacted its users and its engineers were working with Microsoft.

stories.title: Pakistan’s mineral exploration increasingly focused on strategic resources, minister tells investors
summary: Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Friday that Pakistan’s exploration efforts were increasingly focused on minerals that were of strategic importance to global investors.
He was addressing the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF26) in Islamabad, where delegations, exhibitors and attendees have arrived from across the world to attend the event.

As the two-day event opened on Thursday, Pakistan showcased its vast mineral resources, ranging from coal and salt to gold and critical minerals, to attract international investment, promising predictable, investor-friendly policies, institutional support and security.

stories.title: Delhi overtakes Lahore as world's most polluted major city as air quality deteriorates
summary: India’s capital, Delhi, overtook Lahore to become the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with air quality reaching hazardous levels and visibility dropping as smog blanketed the city of 20 million people.

Earlier, Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) stood at 334, categorised as “hazardous”, making it the most polluted major city globally, according to Swiss air quality monitoring group IQAir, which measures pollution levels based on the concentration of pollutants.
Earlier this week, Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration was eight times the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) guideline value, according to a report by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI).

stories.title: Democratic US Senator Chris Van Hollen announces run for US Senate majority leader, challenging Schumer
summary: Democratic US Senator Chris Van Hollen said on Thursday he would run for Senate majority leader, challenging Chuck Schumer, who has led the Democrats in the Senate since 2017, after the Democratic Party won a majority in the chamber in the midterm elections.

Schumer, who is expected to retain his party’s leadership in the chamber but previously predicted not having a challenger, released his own statement on Thursday saying he had the votes to continue as the Democratic leader in the Senate.

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, an independent who caucuses with Democrats, said they would support Van Hollen, who has been a US senator for nearly a decade and spent 14 years before that in the House of Representatives.

stories.title: Security forces kill 74 terrorists during IBOs in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan: ISPR
summary: Security forces have killed 74 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Balochistan, said a statement by the military’s media wing on Friday.

stories.title: Sindh CM calls for accelerated completion of climate-resilient projects
summary: KARACHI: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Thursday directed the provincial departments to speed up water security and climate-resilient projects.

The chief minister directed the irrigation department to maintain the improved flood-protection infrastructure, expedite ongoing drainage schemes and ensure efficient use of available water resources.

The chief minister said that the provincial government would continue to place communities at the centre of its climate-resilience strategy, ensuring that development initiatives deliver lasting improvements in people’s lives.

stories.title: Joint investigation team seizes pistol of Mir Raza’s business partner
summary: KARACHI: The Joint Investigation Team (JIT), formed by the Sindh government, to probe the mysterious death of a young businessman, Mir Raza Ali, has seized the licensed pistol of his partner.
Without naming the partner, West DIG Irfan Baloch, who heads the JIT, said on Thursday that the North Nazimabad branch of Mir Raza’s food chain has also been sealed for further investigation.
The JIT was formed on the recommendation of the judicial commission headed by a Sindh High Court judge to probe the alleged murder of Mir Raza.

stories.title: Lahore High Court moved against change of names of universities
summary: LAHORE: A petition has been filed in the Lahore High Court, challenging the removal of the word “university” from the names of six public sector varsities and demanding restoration of their former title of “college”.

The petition contends that the amendment arbitrarily downgraded the nomenclature of the institutions without consulting the stakeholders, including vice chancellors, faculty members, academic bodies and students.

It claims the change could also create complications for the graduates seeking employment, higher education and immigration-related credential verification abroad, as their degrees and academic records carry the previous university names.

stories.title: OECD report reveals migration to developed countries is dwindling
summary: PARIS: Migration to developed countries dwindled for a second year in a row in 2025, down 1.6pc compared to the previous year, according to an OECD report published on Thursday.
The United States saw a 14pc drop, although it still leads OECD countries, recording more than 1.2m permanent migrants in 2025.
The 1.1m asylum applications in 2025 marked a 22pc decrease to OECD countries, excluding the United States, compared with the previous year, although remaining about 10pc higher than 2019 figures.

stories.title: Two arrested after pet lioness kills farmhouse worker in Lahore's Kahna
summary: LAHORE: A farmhouse owner and a TikToker were arrested on Thursday after a 19-year-old farmhouse employee was killed by a pet lioness in the farmhouse in the Kahna area on Thursday.
A spokesperson for the office of the deputy inspector general (DIG) of police identified the arrested suspects as farmhouse owner Fayyaz and TikToker Nauman.
The spokesperson said Nauman had visited the farmhouse to make a TikTok video when the lioness allegedly went out of control and attacked Talha, a farm employee, leaving him critically injured.

stories.title: Rain, snowfall disrupt life across GB
summary: GILGIT: Intermittent rain and snowfall have created difficulties for residents of Gilgit-Baltistan, with heavy snowfall and landslides blocking the Babusar Pass, Shimshal Valley and several other link roads.
Intermittent snowfall was reported in the upper areas of Gilgit, Diamer, Ghizer, Astore, Skardu, Hunza, Nagar, Khar-mang, Shigar and Ghanche on Thursday, creating difficulties for local residents.
Residents of upper areas are facing transportation difficulties as roads have become hazardous for travel, while temperatures have dropped to zero degrees Celsius.

stories.title: Consumer courts can’t hear insurance policyholder's complaints, LHC holds
summary: Justice Jawad Hassan issued the ruling on a petition filed by the United Insurance Company of Pakistan Limited against an order passed by the District Consumer Court in Bhakkar.
The consumer court had overruled an objection raised by the insurance firm regarding the maintainability of a complaint filed by a policyholder.

Setting aside the consumer court’s order, Justice Hassan observed that the lower forum failed to properly examine the relevant statutory framework, specifically Section 122 of the Insurance Ordinance, 2000.

stories.title: BHC orders govt to determine salaries of local govt representatives
summary: A two-member bench comprising Justice Iqbal Ahmed Kasi and Justice Mian Muhammad Rauf Atta, who authored the judgement, heard a constitutional petition filed by the elected chairman of Mastung Municipal Committee.

The petitioner argued that Section 35 of the Balochistan Local Government Act, 2010, entitled chairmen and vice-chairmen to remuneration, but they had received no salaries or allowances despite performing their duties.
The court also directed authorities to consider appropriate remuneration for elected representatives in view of their statutory responsibilities.

stories.title: CM Bugti assures investors of security in Balochistan
summary: He said the provincial government would provide comprehensive security, a one-window operation and all necessary facilities to investors across the province, including those operating in the Mineral Corridor, adding that there would be no room for red tape.

CM Bugti said people were central to investment and security, adding that the people of Balochistan welcomed national and international partners and wanted investors to benefit from the opportunities available in the province.

Inviting investors to participate in this project as well as other industrial and mineral ventures, he said the government would ensure security and provide all necessary civic and basic facilities in accordance with investors’ requirements.

stories.title: Pakistan calls for ‘immediate’ end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as UNSC renews Yemen sanctions
summary: WASHINGTON: Pakistan called for the “immediate and unconditional” cessation of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia on Thursday, as the United Nations Security Council adopted a resolution renewing sanctions against individuals and entities threatening peace and stability in Yemen.

The resolution also sought to restrict the Houthis’ access to components and chemicals used in manufacturing drones and missiles, and condemned their military escalation inside Yemen, as well as attacks against Saudi Arabia.

Adopted by consensus, it extended the targeted asset freeze and travel ban on individuals threatening peace in Yemen. including those associated with the Houthis, until Nov 14, 2027, and renewed the mandate of the Panel of Experts monitoring the sanctions until Dec 15, 2027.

stories.title: National Assembly panel calls for easing rules for pilgrimage organisers
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Nat­ional Assembly Standing Committee on Religious Affairs on Thursday directed the religious affairs ministry to submit the Zaireen (pilgrims) Management Policy to the panel to help identify gaps in its implementation.
The committee recommended reducing the se­­c­u­rity deposit required from organisers to ease the fi­­n­ancial burden on pilgrims.

Expressing concern over the Rs1 million security deposit imposed on organisers, particularly small-scale operators, the committee recommended reviewing and reducing the amount to ease their financial burden.

stories.title: Work in full swing to plug crater at Tarbela project site
summary: HARIPUR: The civil work, meant to plug the crater caused by the collapse of a weak rock mass in the intake pit area of the Tarbela Dam 5th Extension Hydropower Project (T-5), is in full swing.

On Monday morning, a weak rock mass collapsed during excavation of the 2nd Bench Connecting Tunnel, causing water from the intake pit to enter the tunnel and the powerhouse area of the T-5 project, said an official handout.

Official sources and Haripur district administration said water from the intake pit had been completely drained; no further water was entering the downstream work sites, and dewatering of the under-construction powerhouse had started.

Meanwhile Waleed Bilal produced a blistering back-nine surge to card a two-over-par 74 and take a two-stroke lead in the Men's Amateur category after the opening round.

After struggling to a 42 on the front nine, Bilal ignited his round on the inward half, firing a 32 highlighted by back-to-back twos on the 11th and 12th holes followed by six consecutive fours to close out his day.

stories.title: FCC orders settlement of land compensation claims within six months
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) ruled on Thursday that the Capital Development Authority (CDA), being a creature of the CDA Ordinance, 1960, cannot exercise powers or confer benefits beyond those granted by the statute.

The controversy related to the CDA’s prolonged failure to discharge its statutory obligations under the CDA Ordinance, including non-payment of acquisition compensation, non-allotment of alternative plots, denial of rehabilitation benefits and non-development of acquired sectors.
The FCC highlighted that the CDA was a statutory body constituted under the CDA Ordinance, 1960, for the planning and development of Islamabad.

stories.title: Court to take up CDA’s plea against Bari Imam House stay
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday accepted an application filed by the Capital Development Authority (CDA), seeking vacation of an interim order restraining it from demolishing a structure known as Bari Imam House.
The authority argued that the disputed property was part of land acquired by it in 1963 and had no legal connection with the shrine of Hazrat Bari Imam.
The authority contended that the disputed structure, spread over more than 300 kanals of land, had no connection with the actual site of the shrine of Hazrat Bari Imam.

stories.title: Govt seeks to transform Islamabad’s education system: minister
summary: ISLAMABAD: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal has said that the government was working to transform Islamabad’s education system into a model that can serve as a benchmark for other parts of the country.
He observed that the traditional education system, shaped by colonial-era practices, had placed excessive emphasis on memorisation rather than independent thinking and intellectual development.

Clarifying the scope of the ICT education reforms, the minister said the initiative was aimed at bringing fundamental improvements in teaching practices and learning outcomes rather than merely introducing administrative changes.
